subject: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan (Brightline Health)
body:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is ready to move forward conditional on two items: 1) confirmation of the subprocessor list and 2) agreement on DPA redlines around data residency for our EHR export. I've attached our redlines and the vendor questionnaire — please confirm who at Redwood will review the subprocessor chain and provide evidence for SOC2 scoping.

Elena
Director, Vendor Risk
Brightline Health

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front:
- Subprocessor list: attached CSV (current as of 2026-09-30) — includes edge cache providers and our managed infra partner (CloudVendorCo).
- SOC2 evidence: Laura (cc'd) will share the relevant report excerpts and scope notes.
- DPA residency clause: we can propose a limited carve for EHR exports to be stored in the US-only partition; details below.

Action items I propose:
1) Laura to circulate SOC2 scope and confirm whether the relevant subprocessor appears in our in-scope inventory (target: 2 business days).
2) Redwood legal to propose alternate DPA wording that limits storage/backup locations for EHR exports to the US or approved EU regions (target: initial draft in 3 business days).
3) If CloudVendorCo requires separate flow-down consent, we will route a brief change notice to them and request written acceptance.

Attaching: OrderForm_v3_markedup.docx (our starting point) and Brightline_DPA_redlines_2026-09-27.pdf (their changes).

Thanks — I will coordinate and loop you in on the legal draft.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Elena / Logan —

I reviewed the redlines and the subprocessor CSV. Preliminary notes:
- SOC2: We can provide the Type II report and the subservice organization listing; attached excerpts show CloudVendorCo included for compute and logging.
- DPA redline on residency: Brightline's proposed absolute prohibition on backups outside the US is difficult given our multi-region failover policies. We can offer a compromise: (a) primary storage and backups for EHR exports in US-only regions; (b) failover replication to other regions only with documented encryption-at-rest/transport and with prior notice to Brightline and a maximum 30-day retention in the failover region unless an ongoing incident requires it.
- Subprocessor flow-down: CloudVendorCo has a standing MSA with flow-down language; we will need their written acknowledgment of Brightline's residency exception. I can prepare a one-page change notice template for CloudVendorCo to sign.

Proposed timeline: legal draft of DPA language by Fri 09/30; CloudVendorCo notice out by Mon 10/03; SOC2 package delivered to Brightline by Wed 10/05.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudvendorco.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Logan/Laura —

We got the heads-up about Brightline's residency requirement. Short answer: we can accept a targeted flow-down for their EHR export buckets under a signed change notice; two caveats: (1) we need a scoped indemnity carveout to cover (tiny) costs if we must allocate dedicated hardware; (2) we will require a minimum 6-month lead time for any dedicated provisioning.

I'll review Laura's one-page notice once shared. I can also provide the specific subprocessor attachments you requested.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Product Ops | CloudVendorCo

Attachment stub referenced: provider_capacity_matrix.xlsx (mentioned in body; sent in separate reply)

---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlinehealth.com>, procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, samir.patel@cloudvendorco.com
Bcc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Elena —

Quick update: Laura's DPA draft is attached. Key items:
- Residency compromise language (US primary + flagged failover rules).
- Flow-down path: one-page change notice template for CloudVendorCo to accept (also attached).
- Evidence bundle: SOC2 excerpt + subprocessor listing (PDF).

Could you confirm whether Brightline can accept the proposed failover wording? If so, we will send the change notice to CloudVendorCo and request their written acceptance. If you need a stronger guarantee (e.g., dedicated tenancy), please let us know — Samir outlined capacity and timing implications below.

Next steps:
- Elena to confirm residency acceptance or request dedicated tenancy (reply required by Tue 10/05).
- If accepted, Laura to send change notice to Samir (target Mon 10/03) and collect signed acknowledgment.
- Marissa to update Order Form (pricing delta if dedicated tenancy applies) and circulate updated PO line.

Thanks,
Logan

---

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier chain authorization + DPA onboarding plan

Logan/Team —

We discussed internally. Brightline can accept the failover compromise (US primary + controlled failover with 30-day cap) provided CloudVendorCo signs the change notice and we get a written confirmation of the minimum retention controls. We are not requesting dedicated tenancy at this time, but we reserve the right to revisit at renewal.

Please proceed with the change notice routing. We'll expect the SOC2 excerpts in the same thread as the signed notice.

Elena

---

Thread attachments (referenced):
- Brightline_DPA_redlines_2026-09-27.pdf (external redlines)
- OrderForm_v3_markedup.docx (starting order form)
- subprocessor_list_2026-09-30.csv (Redwood current subprocessor inventory)
- provider_capacity_matrix.xlsx (CloudVendorCo capacity notes; sent separately)

Notes for Redwood internal ops:
- Laura: please mark any subprocessor that is hosting customer PII as "in-scope" in the subprocessor CSV and highlight CloudVendorCo rows for quick review.
- Marissa: prepare two quote lines in the Order Form — (A) standard multi-tenant pricing; (B) US-only dedicated tenancy premium with a 6-month lead time (do not publish pricing publicly).
- Vivek: review whether our routing policies and KV cache replication can guarantee the 30-day cap on failover retention without code changes; flag any blocker ASAP.

--
This email thread is stored in mailbox: logan_wright (Inbox / Procurement).
